name: Otto Happel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2002-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Otto Happel, who studied engineering, inherited his father's dust-removal business and turned it into thermal engineering firm GEA.
In 1999, he sold his 50.1% GEA stake to Germany's MG Technologies for around $775 million in cash and kept a 10% interest in the combined group.
In 2005, the company renamed itself GEA Group. Happel cashed out in 2006, selling his remaining stake to institutional investors for $700 million.
In 2015, he attended the World Economic Forum in his role as chairman of the Swiss private wealth management firm Luserve AG.
forbes_facts: A foundation in his name supports projects in the developing world.
He has a super-yacht named Hetairos and lives in Switzerland with his wife and six children.

name: Michiel Le Roux
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Michiel Le Roux of South Africa founded Capitec Bank in 2001 and owns about 11% of the company's shares.
The bank, which trades on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, targets South Africa's emerging middle class.
He served as chairman of the board of Capitec from 2007 to 2016 and still sits on the company's board.
Le Roux previously ran Boland Bank, a small regional bank in Cape Town's hinterland.
forbes_facts: Capitec Bank has more than 800 branches and over 15,000 employees.
Le Roux was the largest donor to the Democratic Alliance, a liberal South African political party, during its 2023-2024 financial year.

name: John Pritzker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: John Pritzker learned the hotel business at his family's Hyatt Hotel chain; he sold his shares in Hyatt to relatives in 2010.
Pritzker went on to build Commune Hotels and Resorts, a boutique hotel management company, which after a merger in 2016 became Two Roads Hospitality.
In November 2018, Hyatt Hotels purchased Two Roads Hospitality for $408 million.
John's brother Tom Pritzker is the chairman of Hyatt and his sister Gigi Pritzker is a film producer.
A photography buff, he gave $25 million to create the Pritzker Center for Photography at the SFMOMA in San Francisco.
John's father Jay, uncle Robert and grandfather A.N. Pritzker built a diverse fortune that included manufacturing and service group Marmon Holdings.
forbes_facts: Pritzker, a former Dead Head, took time off between high school and college to be part of the emerging counterculture in San Francisco.
To support himself after high school, Pritzker got a union job pulling cables for cable TV in an apartment complex south of San Francisco.

name: Li Hongxin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2005-2026)
forbes_bio: Li chairs Sun Paper, a paper and pulp producer based in Yanzhou, located in the Shandong Province in Eastern China.
Born into a poor peasant family, Li worked at a train station as a porter at the age of 18.
In 1983, he borrowed 30,000 yuan to set up paper producer Sun Paper in his hometown Yanzhou.

name: Karin Sartorius-Herbst
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Karin Sartorius-Herbst inherited a stake in Sartorius AG, which makes pharmaceutical an laboratory equipment.
Her great-grandfather Florenz Sartorius founded what become Sartorius AG in 1870 to make analytical balances to measure small mass in laboratories.
Her father, Horst Sartorius, died in 1998 and left a 50% stake to his daughters Karin, Christine Franken and Ulrike Baro.
An executor oversees their inheritance until 2028.
Today, the company has more than 15,000 employees and annual revenue exceeding $5 billion. It went public in 1990.
forbes_facts: Sartorius-Herbst has had roles in various voluntary endeavors and charitable entities throughout her life.
She studied economics at the University of Goettingen.

name: Lalit Khaitan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Liquor baron Lalit Khaitan is chairman of publicly traded spirits maker Radico Khaitan.
The Delhi-based company started off as a bottler before expanding into making bulk alcohol and eventually branded spirits.
Radico Khaitan has a range of brands including 8 M whisky, Contessa rum and Magic Moments vodka.
Khaitan inherited the liquor business from his later father G.N.Khaitan in 1995 after a family division.
forbes_facts: Khaitan's son Abhishek runs Radico Khaitan as managing director.
The company used to be called Rampur Distillery and Chemical Company.

name: Alexander Svetakov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Alexander Svetakov is one of the biggest property owners in the Moscow region, with most of his land in New Moscow.
Svetakov got his start importing electronics from Asia.
He sold one of his earlier businesses, Absolut bank, in 2007 for $1.4 billion, then a record for Russia's banking sector.
His investment group Absolut had businesses in everything from real estate to caviar extraction.
He sold his caviar business few years ago and concentrated on residential real estate.
forbes_facts: Svetakov enjoys surfing and tennis, and has built tennis courts in Zhukovka cottage village.
Svetakov financed the construction of a school for disabled children near Moscow.

name: Abhay Soi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun India (2019)
forbes_bio: Former finance professional Abhay Soi is chairman and managing director of Max Healthcare Institute, India's second-largest listed hospital chain by revenue.
Soi started his career at the erstwhile Arthur Andersen and later worked for EY and KPMG.
Soi got his entrepreneurial break in 2010 when he took over a struggling 650-bed hospital in Delhi and set up Radiant Life Care.
Radiant was merged with Max in June 2020 and listed two months later.
He's looking to double the number of hospital beds by 2029.

name: Ami Luttwak
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2025)
forbes_bio: Ami Luttwak cofounded Israeli cloud security business Wiz and owned a 10% stake in the company.
Google's parent company Alphabet acquired Wiz for $32 billion in cash in March 2026.
Wiz software scans storage providers such as Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure to flag and prioritize security risks.
The company's revenue surpassed $100 million in 2023, when the founders began their "suicide plan" of hiring fast, raising funds and targeting top-of-market corporations.
Wiz customers include Fox, Morgan Stanley and LVMH, whose billionaire CEO wrote the unicorn a personal check.

name: Shuo Wang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2022-2026); Hurun Global (2025-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Hurun China U40 (2022); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Shuo Wang is cofounder and chief revenue officer of HR software company Deel.
In 2019, Wang started Deel with MIT classmate Alex Bouaziz to make it easier for companies to hire employees globally.
Deel raised funding at a $17.3 billion valuation in October 2025 and surpassed $1 billion in annual recurring revenue earlier in the year.
Wang moved to the U.S. from China when she was 16, then studied mechanical engineering with a focus on robotics at MIT.
After college, Wang cofounded and was chief technology officer of air purifier maker Aeris; iRobot bought it in 2021 for around $100 million.

name: Roberta Armani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Roberta Armani is the niece of billionaire fashion designer Giorgio Armani (d. September 2025) and the daughter of his late brother Sergio Armani.
She is a board member of Armani's namesake fashion firm and holds the title of head of global and VIP communications, leading the brand's partnerships with Hollywood stars.
Under the terms of Armani's will, Roberta is entitled to 17% of the net proceeds from the sale or public listing of 45% of the company within five years of Armani's death.
She also inherited some of Armani's shares in eyewear giant EssilorLuxottica.
